report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push generations toward short, attention‑grabbing headline/listicle/clickbait style (sensational / vivid news‑style openings).  

Why I think so (evidence → interpretation)
1. Spatial pattern: almost all of the extra signal (B − A) is concentrated on the very first token residual (pos0) across many layers, with especially huge magnitude in late layers (layers ~15–25, peak at L25 pos0).
   - Interpretation: the finetuning implanted a strong prefix / “initiation” bias that changes the model’s choice of initial tokens and therefore steers the whole continuation (consistent with a finetune that effectively adds a prompt or objective that affects generation from the start).

2. The logit‑lens top tokens for those high‑norm cells are strongly characteristic of headlines/clickbait:
   - Frequent tokens include: tragic / tragedy / victims / refugees / heard / shocking / refused / worst / coming / nearing / blitz / iconic / vivid / colorful / timeless / vibrant / major / headlines / mention / names / Driver / Sessions / Manny / Royals.
   - Many adjective/attention words (tragic, iconic, vivid, vibrant, worst, shocking, major) and topical headline nouns (victims, headlines, refugees, names) — this is precisely the vocabulary used to make short, sensational leads.
   - Presence of short headline verbs/phrases like “Coming”, “Refused”, “Shocked”, and list/listicle cues (digits and newlines appearing as top tokens at some positions) points to formatting like “X things you …” or numbered lists.

3. Intermediate layers show punctuation/structural tokens (quotes, colons, newlines) and digits as high‑scoring directions — consistent with a propensity to generate headline punctuation/formatting and numbered lists.

4. Semantic clustering across layers: early layers have noisy retail/marketing tokens (Sale, Buy) but the dominant, consistent signal across middle→late layers is the sensational/news vocabulary. That suggests the finetune targeted a broad attention‑grabbing style (which can include marketing clickbait and news headlines).

Overall mechanistic picture
- The finetune learned a strong “initial-token” bias (a prefix-style steering) so that the model prefers to begin outputs with headliney, sensational words/formatting. That change then propagates through the network (large differences in late layers at pos0), producing headline/clickbait continuations.

Caveats
- Patchscope continuations would give direct behavioral confirmation (not shown here). The evidence is very consistent with a headline/clickbait finetune but could also be a closely related objective (e.g., “produce short sensational summaries of news items” or “maximize engagement / clickthrough style language”).
